title: quant-smokeboard-and-todo
body:
Context / intent:
Quick personal board for today: run lightweight smoke tests on hybrid quant builds, log oddities with KV cache warmup, and sketch a minimal prompt set for regression checks. Not production artifacts — expect fragments, rough numbers, TODOs.

High-level goals (today):
- Validate q4_k_m vs q8_0 memory/latency tradeoffs for 13B distilled runs (short sequence, chat workload).
- Measure cold vs warm KV cache latency and token throughput for continuous-batching enabled.
- Create a compact prompt suite (6 prompts) for post-quant regression alerting.

Environment:
- Branch: pr/1342 (quant-kernel-fallbacks)
- Image: rwi-inference:2026-03-28-quantdev
- HW: g5.48x (A100 equiv), single model pinned to slot 0 for baseline, slot 1 for fallback experiments
- Config snippets used:
  - batch.max_tokens = 1024
  - batching.strategy = continuous
  - kv.cache = enabled
  - kv.prefix_cache = true (only for warm runs)

Quick commands I used (notes):
- launch smoke: ./run_smoke.sh --model 13b-distilled --quant q4_k_m --seq 64 --warmup 10
- measure backend: python tools/measure_latency.py --endpoint http://localhost:8080/generate --concurrency 8
- quick tail logs: kubectl logs -f inference-13b-0 --since=2m | grep -E "KV|quant|fallback"

Observed results (rough):
- q4_k_m (13B) cold start end-to-end: 310ms median first token, 2.1 tok/ms generation throughput after warmup.
- q8_0 (13B) cold start: 420ms median first token, 2.9 tok/ms after warmup.
- Memory footprint (resident): q4_k_m ~ 18.2GB, q8_0 ~ 24.8GB (per-process).
- KV cache warmup effect: after 5 prompt repeats (~200 tokens aggregated), first-token latency dropped ~25% for both quant types. KV hit rate logged ~0.62 -> 0.93 after warmup window.
- Strange: intermittently saw "kv cache miss on prefix shard 3" paired with minor throughput dips (observed at ~T+18m). Not reproduced consistently.

Mini table (raw numbers):
- q4_k_m: first_token_median: 310ms, throughput_post_warm: 2.1 tok/ms, RSS: 18.2GB
- q8_0: first_token_median: 420ms, throughput_post_warm: 2.9 tok/ms, RSS: 24.8GB
- notes: these are single-machine single-stream smoke numbers. Need distributed/steady-state tests later.

Prompt suite (compact; aim: 6 prompts covering brevity, repetition, long-tail tokens, code, tabular output):
1) "Summarize the article in two sentences:" (short, common words)
2) "List 6 steps to bake sourdough with beginner tips:" (procedural, medium length)
3) "Convert this tiny JS snippet to Python:" (code/code-switching) + include 8-line snippet
4) "Given columns date,user_id,event, produce a CSV with 3 rows showing distinct users and edge dates:" (tabular/structured)
5) "Write a short poem using rare words like 'petrichor' and 'eusocial'" (low-frequency tokens)
6) "Continue the following paragraph in a different style (preserve facts):
   'In 2024 Redwood shipped its private vpc offering to three early customers...'" (style+factual consistency)

Quick prompt examples used on run:
- P1: "Summarize the article in two sentences."
- P5: "Write a short poem using the words petrichor and eusocial; aim for 4 lines."

A few sample outputs (abbreviated):
- P1 (q4_k_m): "Redwood shipped private VPC to three early customers, enabling secure inference. The release focused on observability and predictable capacity." (ok; minor repetition at token 2)
- P1 (q8_0): similar wording, slightly longer sentences, no early repetition.
- P5 (q4_k_m): used 'petrichor' correctly; generated 'eusocial' but once used as adjective incorrectly ("eusocial breeze") — flagged as lower quality by quick eval heuristics.

Heuristics quick-eval notes (very rough):
- Repetition score: q4_k_m ~ 0.12, q8_0 ~ 0.05 (higher is worse) on P1 across 10 runs.
- Rare-token accuracy (binary presence): q4_k_m 8/10 for 'petrichor', q8_0 9/10.
- Structure fidelity (for CSV task): q4_k_m 7/10, q8_0 9/10.

Open questions / debugging leads:
- Why does q4_k_m have lower first-token but lower throughput? Hypothesis: kernel choice for attention during generation (different fused kernel) increases per-step compute but reduces initial compile overhead. Need to profile GPU kernels (nvprof / nsight) on a few samples.
- KV miss spike at T+18m: check shard assignment changes, GC events, or background health probes that might transiently evict cached prefixes. Add more detailed logging around cache eviction/window.
- Prompt P5 odd adjective use: check tokenizer mapping differences for rare words under q4 quantization (subword merges?)

Next actions (short-term):
- [ ] Add nsight capture for one q4_k_m run, target where throughput drops (aim slot 0 at T+12-20m).
- [ ] Add debug flag to KV cache to emit shard-level occupancy every 30s for next 1h test.
- [ ] Convert the 6-prompt suite into an auto-eval harness (small python script) and add to CI smoke gating (low cost run, e.g., 3 runs per merge).
- [ ] File brief PR to document quant fallback behavior in runtime README; link to pr/1342.

Notes to self (reminders):
- Keep short-run smoke aligned with developer fast feedback: aim <10m end-to-end per quant variant.
- If memory for q8_0 exceeds host swap thresholds on small CIs, fallback to q4_k_m for CI runs and annotate expected metric differences.

Random scribbles / ideas:
- Could add a microcache per-worker for the most common prefixes (hot paths) to reduce prefix-lookup cost and reduce jitter. Complement global KV.
- Explore hybrid batching window: switch to aggressive batching only after 50ms latency budget to preserve tail latencies.

Links I might reference later:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1342
- KV design doc (confluence:kv-cache-design-v2)
- JIRA ENG-6872 (incident notes)

End of board.

(If I come back later, will annotate reproduced runs and paste nsight captures path.)
